snippet.title: Is Betelgeuse Really About to Explode?
snippet.description:
Is Betelgeuse About to Explode?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vP1BbqZ_dnM

The orange star on Orion's shoulder is a dying red supergiant. One day Betelgeuse will blow itself apart as a supernova and shine so brightly for weeks that it will be visible in the daytime sky — but what do the 2019 Great Dimming and seismic models say about when?

Sources: Joyce et al. (2020), The Astrophysical Journal 902, 63 — Betelgeuse radius, mass, distance and core helium-burning stage (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/abb8db) · Montargès et al. (2021), Nature 594, 365–368 — the 2019–2020 Great Dimming dust veil (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03546-8) · Goldberg, Bauer & Howell (2020), Research Notes of the AAS 4, 35 — Type IIP supernova plateau brightness at half-Moon scale (https://doi.org/10.3847/2515-5172/ab7c68).

Pictures: ESO/B. Tafreshi (twanight.org), R. Wesson/ESO, ESO/S. Brunier, and ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO) Orion and observatory time-lapses (CC BY 4.0), and ESO/M. Montargès et al. VLT/SPHERE image of Betelgeuse (CC BY 4.0), alongside original animated explainers and AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: ESO/B. Tafreshi (twanight.org, CC BY 4.0); R. Wesson/ESO (CC BY 4.0); ESO/S. Brunier (CC BY 4.0); ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO, CC BY 4.0); ESO/M. Montargès et al. (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

snippet.title: Is Betelgeuse About to Explode? (We'd See It in the Daytime Sky)
snippet.description:
Is Betelgeuse about to explode? Betelgeuse is a dying red supergiant star on Orion's shoulder — and when it explodes, it will shine in daylight.

Follow the VLT and Hubble observations behind the Great Dimming, the physics of core collapse, how bright a Betelgeuse supernova will shine from Earth, and what seismic models say about how much time the star has left.

Chapters
0:00 A dying star in Orion
0:37 The Star in Orion's Shoulder
1:45 The Great Dimming
2:50 How a Giant Star Dies
4:08 The Night It Goes
5:43 So When Will It Explode?

Sources: Joyce et al. (2020), The Astrophysical Journal 902, 63 — Betelgeuse radius, mass, distance and core helium-burning stage (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/abb8db); Montargès et al. (2021), Nature 594, 365–368 — the 2019–2020 Great Dimming dust veil and cool photospheric patch (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03546-8); Dupree et al. (2022), The Astrophysical Journal 936, 18 — the surface mass ejection and 400-day pulsation reset (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/ac7853); Goldberg, Bauer & Howell (2020), Research Notes of the AAS 4, 35 — Type IIP supernova plateau brightness at half-Moon scale (https://doi.org/10.3847/2515-5172/ab7c68); Howell et al. (2025), The Astrophysical Journal Letters — tentative speckle-imaging detection of Betelgeuse's companion star (https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.15749).
